newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius says IFOR, Hungary fest helped up profit.
newsitem.headline: Danubius says IFOR, Hungary fest helped up profit.

text.p: Hungarian hotel group Danubius Rt said in its earnings report on Monday that an increase in utilisation of its Budapest hotels was one of the reasons for rising 1996 profits at its core hotels.

After discounting for changes in its room capacity, utilisation grew by 7.3 percent compared to 1995 because of an increase in tourism caused by Hungary's 1,100th anniversary celebrations and the use of Danubius hotels by troops of the international Bosnia intervention force (IFOR), it added.
The report did not specify the capacity utilisation at the Budapest hotels but said that nationwide it was 68.4 percent 1996, 2.5 percent more than in 1995.
Danubius Rt reported an unconsolidated pre-tax profit of 2.43 billion forints in 1996, against 2.04 billion in the year before.
The consolidated pre-tax profits of the chain were 2.67 billion forints in 1996 compared to 2.06 billion in 1995.
IFOR troops, whose mandate expired at the end of last year, were often furloughed in Budapest, the major non-Yugoslav city closest to their area of operations.
Outside Budapest, capacity utilisation fell by 2.0 percent, the report said without indicating the 1996 or 1995 figures.

In other matters, the report said that increasing franchise fees charged by Hilton Hotels for the Budapest Hilton Hotel, and consultant fees that occurred in relation to the acquisition of Hungaria Hotels Rt, were the main reasons the chain's expenses increased in 1996.
Danubius bought Hungaria late last year from the privatisation agency APV Rt.
